name: Looksmax.org / forum participation

lead: Looksmax.org is described as one of the main hubs of looksmaxxing, alongside forum.looksmaxxing.com. Members post photos for feedback, ask for ratings and share guides, using the replies as a map for what to improve in their face and body.

The chain is simple: post photos, get a current and 'potential' PSL score from peers, read the shared guides, then apply tips on skin, grooming, fitness or procedures. The feedback comes from peers on a self-devised rating scale, and the guides' methods range from studied to anecdotal.

paras: Members typically post front and side photos, discuss softmaxxing (non-invasive changes) and hardmaxxing (surgery, steroids), and use shared vocabulary such as canthal tilt and hunter eyes. Many post progress photos over months to track changes. Anonymity is common.

Commentators and researchers link the subculture to body dysmorphia, depression and anxiety, promotion of dangerous methods, blackpill determinism and radicalisation. Critics also call the PSL scale unscientific and biased against non-white men. Members often gatekeep against casual 'normies'.

lead: Looksmax.org is an online forum that Grokipedia describes as one of the main later hubs of looksmaxxing, together with forum.looksmaxxing.com, hosting guides, PSL rating threads and rate-me requests [1]. Looksmaxxing, a practice focused on maximising male attractiveness, formed on incel-linked message boards in the 2010s, and Wikipedia names PUAHate, Sluthate and Lookism.net as the 'PSL forums' that created the PSL rating scale [2].

Wikipedia's article does not mention looksmax.org specifically, so the details below about it rest mostly on Grokipedia, an AI-generated source. Female-oriented guides reportedly appeared on the site in 2024 and 2025 [1].
infobox: Guides, PSL rating threads, progress photos

paras: Looksmaxxing took shape on incel-linked boards in the mid-2010s [2][1]. After Reddit banned r/incels in 2017, activity moved to independent forums, often on.is domains, and from around 2020 to TikTok, where it reached non-incel audiences [1].

Members post progress photos and request ratings on current and potential PSL, sometimes using wet-hair photos to reduce styling effects [1]. Ratings are competitive and quantify perceived genetic potential [1]. Anonymity is common, and members gatekeep against casual 'normies' [1]. Core vocabulary includes softmaxxing, hardmaxxing, blackpill, canthal tilt, hunter eyes, mewing and bonesmashing [2][1].

Commentators describe the practice as judgemental and link it to body dysmorphia and suicidal ideation, and researchers say it promotes hegemonic masculinity [2]. Grokipedia lists controversies including blackpill determinism, misogynistic slang, promotion of unproven methods such as bonesmashing and unregulated overseas surgery with reported complications, criticism of PSL as unscientific, and research linking the subculture to radicalisation [1].

timeline.event: Looksmaxxing forms on incel-linked boards such as Lookism.net and Sluthate [2][1].
Reddit bans r/incels, pushing activity to independent forums [1].
